title: Onboard lyra-14b v1.0: perf profiles, metadata, and changelog automation
author: Aisha Kapoor
commits: Initial import: add lyra-14b model artifacts, weights pointer and metadata template
Add performance profiles (latency/throughput/cost) and quantization recommendations
Add changelog automation hooks and release note templates; tests and docs updates
description: This PR onboards lyra-14b v1.0 into the model registry with production-ready metadata, curated performance profiles, and automated changelog/release-note generation. Motivation: Lyra is a high-quality open model we want available in the catalog with verified performance characteristics and opinionated serving recommendations so customers can pick the right variant for cost/latency tradeoffs. Changes include: 1) model metadata (manifest, tags, safety and license fields, recommended runtimes), 2) perf profiles (p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec throughput, memory footprints across GPU families) and quantization recommendations, 3) packaging scripts and CI workflow for validating profile consistency, 4) changelog automation: a lightweight generator that consumes the perf/metadata diffs and emits release notes into the catalog, and 5) docs and quickstart example for Lyra. Checklist: - [x] Add metadata manifest with license/safety fields and example config - [x] Generate perf profiles with unit tests validating formats - [x] Add quantization recommendation file (fp16/q4/awq notes) - [x] Add changelog automation hook and template - [x] Add CI workflow to validate onboarding artifacts - [x] Update docs and quickstart - [x] Run integration tests on Dedicated and Hosted pipelines Testing notes: perf profiles were generated using the perf-lab harness (100 warmup runs, 500 measured runs) and validated against existing profile schema. A small accuracy smoke-check was run with the eval-harness (sanity prompts) to ensure no obvious generation regressions. The changelog generator was exercised locally and via CI to ensure templated release notes are emitted to the /releases directory as part of the release automation flow. Backwards compatibility: metadata fields are additive and follow the registry schema v2. No breaking schema changes. Rollout plan: merge to main will trigger catalog sync and automated release-note draft; ops will promote to hosted catalog after manual spot-checks. See linked linear tasks for rollout coordination.
